answer: Claimants with simple floating thermometers report sea temperature at the same hour, and the values must agree with satellite sea-surface readings for their stretch of coast within a tight band. A ripple on the surface marks the warm shallows, a quill of foam drifts past the rocks, and a harbor wall shelters water a degree warmer than the open sea. One operator cannot fake the gradient from a desk, since the satellite already fixed the pattern and any invented value would stick out.
